A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OHRBench research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained tables, figures, prompts, and case studies can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original OCR/RAG benchmark results, controlled noise experiments, table-format comparisons, and error analyses in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds noise diagnostics, question-rewriting experiments, and comparisons involving VisRAG, Azure OCR, and Ext2Gen.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, Q&A filtering, semantic-noise simulation, and formatting-noise perturbation procedures remain unchanged. VisRAG and Ext2Gen are additional evaluated methods; v3 does not introduce a new proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Appendix IV.2 adds a human-rewritten question scenario using 100 existing Q&As, extending evaluation to different query wording. The seven domains, Chinese/English coverage, document collection, and underlying question tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V3 substantially expands the evaluated comparison methods with VisRAG, commercial Azure OCR, and the robust generator Ext2Gen-8B-R2 in Tables S4–S5. VisRAG was cited in v2 but lacked this reported comparison. The original six OCR solutions remain evaluated.

E3.justification: The main top-2 retrieval protocol, 1,024-token nonoverlapping chunks, and LCS/F1 metrics remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce paired evaluation of 100 original/rewritten questions, a shared Qwen2-VL-7B generator for the VisRAG comparison, Ext2Gen configurations, and block-level OCR-noise measurements.

E4.justification: V3 adds quantitative comparisons of simulated and real OCR-noise distributions in Figure S2, real-output noise-frequency diagnostics in Table S3, question-rewriting robustness in Appendix IV.2, and robust-generator analysis in IV.4. These extend validation beyond v2's retained noise sweeps, format comparisons, error analysis, and case studies.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged. The additions provide no new confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure S2 characterizes variation in document-level OCR errors, rather than uncertainty across repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the renumbered domain tables retain their values, but substantial result sets are added. Table S4 reports VisRAG at 40.2 versus Qwen2.5-VL at 40.6 with the shared Qwen2-VL-7B generator. Table S5 adds Azure and Ext2Gen results. Appendix IV.2 reports rewriting effects, including GT falling from 27.2 to 23.2. These are additional comparisons and conditions, not improvements to the unchanged main results.

T1.justification: The existing perturbation definitions, rates, and LCS-based affected-question criterion remain unchanged. Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs; the added noise diagnostics do not introduce substantive formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark's novelty claim, the two-type noise taxonomy, and the central conclusions about OCR degradation and model-dependent formatting-noise robustness. The additional experiments support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning question-style sensitivity and vision-based RAG limitations. It also hypothesizes that Azure's formatting tags explain Llama3.1-8B's weakness and interprets the remaining gap with Ext2Gen as an OCR bottleneck. The original overarching interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 only promises release of the benchmark's PDFs, Q&As, and ground-truth structured data. V3 reports their release and supplies a repository access link, materially changing documented access to the central research resource. This assesses the PDF's disclosure, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 49 to 58 works, including Ext2Gen and UniMERNet, with additional citations in the introduction and related work. Ext2Gen also receives experimental discussion. The existing related-work narrative and OHRBench's main novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose is largely retained, with limited wording edits, updated author affiliations, and added acknowledgments. Four additional experimental subsections expand the appendix, while the existing section sequence and explanations remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds three supplemental tables and the noise-distribution figure. Figure 1 moves from PDF page 3 to page 2, and appendix numbering and layout adjust around the additions. Existing main figures and all ten case-study image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens evidence about noise realism and question-style robustness, adds informative VisRAG/Azure/Ext2Gen comparisons, and reports benchmark release. These gains are limited by the 100-question rewriting sample and limited protocol and uncertainty reporting for the additions. The introduction's broad 14% gap wording also warrants clearer scoping: Table S5 shows smaller generator-specific Azure gaps, whereas the retained Table 2 averages generators.
